Heatmap of cross correlations X x Y, optionally partial

Source: R/plot_heatmap.R
plot_cor_cross.Rd

Either computes the correlations (cor_cross()) or draws an existing cor_cross object passed as data.

Usage

plot_cor_cross(
  data,
  x_vars,
  y_vars,
  covariates = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  p_adjust = "BH",
  adjust_by = c("y", "x", "all", "none"),
  meth = c("spearman", "pearson", "kendall"),
  engine = c("ppcor", "base"),
  base_size = 10,
  title = NULL,
  value_size = 2.8,
  show_note = TRUE,
  bin_mark = " [0/1]",
  split_binary = TRUE,
  palette = COR_PAL,
  caption_width = 90,
  ci = 0.95
)

Arguments

data

data frame, or the output of cor_cross()

x_vars

predictors (rows of the heatmap, e.g. biomarkers)

y_vars

outcomes (columns, e.g. scores)

covariates

covariates of the partial correlation (NULL = unadjusted)

labels

named vector variable -> display label

p_adjust

method of stats::p.adjust()

adjust_by

family of the adjustment: "y" (the predictors of each score, default, as in univariable forest plots), "x" (the scores of each predictor), "all" (every test), "none"

meth

"spearman" (default), "pearson" or "kendall"

engine

"ppcor" (default) or "base" for the partial correlations

base_size

base font size

title

title (default " correlations")

value_size

size of the values

show_note

add the short reading note for binary variables to the caption

bin_mark

marker appended to the labels of binary variables

split_binary

binary variables in a separate facet ("Continuous" / "Binary 0/1")

palette

colours of the negative / positive correlations (named low / high)

caption_width

wrap the caption lines at this number of characters (NULL = no wrapping); ~60 for two heatmaps side by side

ci

confidence level (NULL = none)

Value

list(table, plot, note): table = the table of cor_cross() (usable by tbl_cor_cross() and tbl_cor_long()); note = full reading note for binary variables (NULL if none)

Examples

d <- simulate_cor_data(150)
res <- plot_cor_cross(d, x_vars = c("CRP", "IL6", "NfL", "BIN_CRP", "BIN_IL6"),
                      y_vars = c("depression", "fatigue", "cognition"),
                      covariates = c("age", "sex"), labels = attr(d, "labels"))
res$plot
